extracted.intended_audience: fact-checking organizations, fact-checkers, and journalists worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: High-level standards, programs, and commitments promoted by the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) for organizations and individuals involved in fact-checking, including principles, transparency, safety, training, and funding support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: For organizations that aspire to abide by our commitment to fact-checking excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN's flagship standard/pledge for organizations; the homepage invites organizations to 'Read our pledge to facts' (linking to the full Code). The page frames this as the primary commitment organizations should adopt to signal adherence to IFCN's norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Build trust in the IFCN that fosters global collaboration with certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN highlights transparency as a core dimension for trust-building and global collaboration; the homepage links to a 'Transparency Statement' that presumably gives concrete disclosure expectations (financial, editorial, methodology) for members/accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information integrity / commitment to fact-checking excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The IFCN advocates for information integrity and supports fact-checking journalists through networking, capacity building and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as the overall mission metric: organizations and practitioners should advance information integrity and accountability in journalism via rigorous fact-checking practices, trend monitoring, and capacity building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-Checkers' Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-Checkers’ Safety (program area listed in site navigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN lists safety of fact-checkers as a distinct area of work — implying standards and guidance around safeguarding practitioners (physical safety, digital security, harassment mitigation) though the homepage only references the program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Master the art of fact-checking and improve your media literacy skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN provides training and resources as a quality/capacity metric: organizations and individuals are expected to use and benefit from IFCN training to improve fact-checking skills and media literacy; homepage links to further materials and expert instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant opportunities / financial sustainability support
rubrics_metrics.description: For fact-checkers seeking fellowships or funding to launch your next big idea. See if you're eligible for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN offers grants and funds (e.g., Global Fact Check Fund) to encourage financial sustainability — positioning financial resilience and diversified funding as an organizational standard/need for healthy fact-checking operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global collaboration and convening (GlobalFact)
rubrics_metrics.description: GlobalFact — the world’s largest annual conference to convene fact-checkers, share resources and explore the field’s future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in global convenings and peer-exchange is presented as a standard practice for strengthening fact-checking quality and community norms; the conference is a mechanism for disseminating best practices and collective standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue-focused alliances (CoronavirusFacts Alliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unite with fact-checkers around the world to publish the truth about COVID-19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IFCN supports thematic/issue alliances as a mode for coordinated quality responses to specific misinformation crises; this implies standards for collaborative fact-checking and coordinated publication for high-impact topics.
